chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you place the deceased in the grave, you say: 'O Allah, this is Your servant and the son of Your servant and the son of Your maid. He has descended to You, and You are the best of those to whom he descends.'

So when you lower him from the direction of the feet and dangle him, you say: 'In the name of Allah and by Allah and upon the religion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). O Allah, to Your mercy, not to Your punishment. O Allah, make spacious for him in his grave, and teach him his proof, and confirm him with the firm word, and protect us and him from the punishment of the grave.'
And when you level the soil over him, you say: 'O Allah, turn the earth away from his sides, and ascend his soul to the souls of the believers in 'Illiyyin, and join him with the righteous.'

key_terms.حُجَّتَهُ: His proof (referring to the Imam or divine argument)
key_terms.عِلِّيِّينَ: Illiyyin (a high register or realm of the righteous)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific prayers to recite when placing a deceased person in the grave according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the ritual supplications recited at three distinct stages of burial, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the deceased's transition through the intermediate realm (barzakh). The phrases 'You are the best of those who take down' and 'confirm him with the firm word' connect the burial rite to broader eschatological themes of divine mercy and the trial of the grave, reinforcing the believer's hope for a favorable reckoning.
